latin: Sicut secretam magiam a nobis primum ex Orphei hymnis elicitam_fas non est in publicum explicare, ita nutu quodam, ut in infrascriptis fiet conclusionibus, eam per amphorismorum capita demonstrasse, utile erit ad excitandas contemplatiuorum mentes.
translation: Just as it is not permitted to set forth publicly the secret magic first drawn out by us from the hymns of Orpheus, so it will be useful, by a kind of hint, as will happen in the conclusions written below, to have shown it through the headings of aphorisms, so as to arouse the minds of contemplatives.
translation_note: 'a nobis primum...elicitam' stakes a claim of originality; Farmer's note reads this claim of priority as aimed at Ficino, whose own commentary on the Orphic Hymns predates Pico's (farmer1998:25645). On Pico's technical use of 'aphorism' Farmer cross-refers to 8>6 and 11>57 (farmer1998:25645).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch17, from Latin at farmer1998:25569
attribution: Pico's own opinion, opening thesis of section 10> (Orphic Hymns) (farmer1998:25569).
doctrine: The thesis states Pico's method for the Orphic Hymns theses that follow: rather than publish the secret magic he claims first to have drawn from the Hymns, he will demonstrate it obliquely, by a 'kind of hint', through the headings of aphorisms (farmer1998:25569).
context: Farmer's note reads Pico's stress on his own originality here as directed against Ficino, 'who years earlier had composed his own commentary on the Hymns' (farmer1998:25645).
historiography: Wirszubski quotes the opening of this thesis verbatim from Pico's Opera, pp. 106-107, connecting it to Pico's stated method of interpreting the Hymns 'secundum Magiam' (wirszubski1989:9987). Busi and Ebgi likewise print the thesis's Latin from the Conclusiones, page 504 (busi2014:17236).
